question.text: Option price can never be negative because:

answer.text: Intrinsic value is at least zero (even for OTM options), and time value is non-negative
SEBI regulations prohibit negative option prices
Exchanges set a floor price for all options
The clearing corporation absorbs losses to prevent negative prices

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, an option price is at least the intrinsic value, and intrinsic value is at least zero - even for OTM options. With time value also non-negative, the total premium cannot become negative. The Trap: The non-negativity is a structural property of the payoff, not a SEBI rule, an exchange-imposed floor, or absorption of losses by the clearing corporation. Note: The workbook illustrates this by pointing out that even when the underlying behaves adversely, the option price still cannot fall below zero, because intrinsic value bottoms out at zero rather than turning negative.
